lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A giant Chain Chomp chained to a peg in Bob-omb Battlefield, close to a cell that holds the Power Star of "Behind Chain Chomp's Gate".

from.quote: A giant Chain Chomp
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: is located on Bob-omb Battlefield in Super Mario 64
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: It is attached to a peg near a cell with the Power Star of
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: You cannot beat it, since Chain Chomps are almost entirely invincible, but a Bob-omb or a box stuns it for a moment.

from.quote: In Super Mario games, they are almost entirely invincible
from.quote_sits_at: General information > Powers and abilities

from.quote: A Bob-omb, a box, or a Yoshi's egg in the remake can stun Chain Chomp briefly.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: Keep away from it: when you are close it lunges, and a hit costs three wedges of health. Pound the ground on its post three times and it breaks free, then rushes into the cell beside it, which clears the mission "Behind Chain Chomp's Gate".

from.quote: The Chain Chomp lunges at Mario if he is nearby, taking away three wedges of his health on contact.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: The Chain Chomp can be freed by ground-pounding its post three times, required for it to lunge into the cell nearby and clear
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A small ghost that follows you in the courtyard of Peach's Castle and in Big Boo's Haunt; touching one takes two wedges of health.

from.quote: Boos (also called Baby Boos) appear in Super Mario 64
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Boos are encountered in the courtyard of Peach's Castle and in Big Boo's Haunt.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Boos take away two wedges of health on contact.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: Any punch, kick or ground pound beats it. Look at one and it fades to half-visible; look away and it is solid again and carries on following you.

from.quote: Boos are defeated from either a punch, a kick, a Pound the Ground attack
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: When Boos are looked at, they become partially visible, but are fully opaque otherwise and follow the player character.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: Each Boo in the courtyard holds a yellow coin, and each one in Big Boo's Haunt holds a blue coin.

from.quote: The Boos in the courtyard hold a Yellow Coin each, and those in Big Boo's Haunt each have a Blue Coin
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: The giant ghost who owns Big Boo's Haunt and leads the Boos; he is the boss of "Go on a Ghost Hunt", "Ride Big Boo's Merry-Go-Round" and "Big Boo's Balcony", and a touch costs three wedges of health.

from.quote: acting as the Boos' leader
from.quote_sits_at: lead (before the first heading)

from.quote: Big Boo makes his debut in Super Mario 64 as the owner of Big Boo's Haunt, being the boss of "Go on a Ghost Hunt", "Ride Big Boo's Merry-Go-Round", and "Big Boo's Balcony".
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: If this Boo attacks Mario, he loses three wedges of health.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: He takes damage only while he is showing. Drop onto him with a ground pound, or hit him with a punch from the side. Three hits finish him, and each hit leaves him smaller and quicker.

from.quote: Big Boo can be attacked only when visible, so Mario has to attack this massive ghost by either ground-pounding him from above or punching him from the side. He takes three hits to defeat, becoming smaller and faster after each hit.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: In the first two missions beat a few of the Boos around him and he appears; in "Big Boo's Balcony" he is already waiting. Like the small Boos he vanishes while you look at him and returns when you look away, and leaving before he is beaten resets his health.

from.quote: For the first two missions, Mario needs to defeat several nearby Boos to make him appear, though for the last one, he is automatically present
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Like with the normal Boos, Big Boo disappears when looked at and becomes visible again when Mario turns away.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: if the player leaves the area before completely defeating Big Boo, his health resets.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: A Big Boo about twice the size of the other Boos waits in a corner of the castle courtyard, and beating it drops a birdcage that leads to Big Boo's Haunt.

from.quote: In the courtyard itself, it can be found in one of the corners, appearing about twice as large as the other Boos. If Mario defeats it, it drops a birdcage
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: leading to Big Boo's Haunt.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A sleepy plant with green lips, found in Whomp's Fortress in the original game, that is always asleep, with a lullaby playing, until you disturb it.

from.quote: They are depicted with green lips in the original version
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Piranha Plants appear only in Whomp's Fortress
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Piranha Plants have a sleepy nature, which is why they are always found asleep; during this, a lullaby plays.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: Walk up slowly and it stays asleep; touch it or rush at it and it wakes and bites toward you.

from.quote: When a Piranha Plant is either touched or approached quickly by the player character, it wakes up and starts to bite in the direction of the player character, though they stay asleep if approached slowly.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: A bite takes three points of health, or four if you have lost your cap. A defeated Piranha Plant leaves a blue coin.

from.quote: Piranha Plants take away three health points if they bite the player character, or four if he is without his cap
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Defeating certain enemies causes a Blue Coin to appear, including Koopa Troopas, Piranha Plants, Boos
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A common walking bomb whose first stop is Bob-omb Battlefield. Get noticed and it ignites its own fuse and runs at you.

from.quote: Bob-ombs are common enemies in Super Mario 64 and its Nintendo DS version. They first appear on the Bob-omb Battlefield.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: When a Bob-omb spots the player, it lights its fuse and then rushes towards them from behind, attempting to damage them when it explodes.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: Walking into one is harmless, but when it blows up it takes two wedges of health. To beat one, kick it, or grab it from behind and toss it; the blast goes off away from you and a coin is left behind.

from.quote: Unlike in the Super Mario Bros. subseries, Bob-ombs do not harm the player upon contact. Their explosion, however, damages the player by two wedges of health.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Bob-ombs can be defeated by being kicked or picked up from behind and thrown. This causes them to explode away from the player, leaving behind a coin.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: Their blasts also hurt other enemies nearby, and they come back after you leave the area.

from.quote: Explosions caused by the bombs can also damage other enemies within the blast.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: After the player character walks away from the area, the Bob-ombs then respawn.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: One Bob-omb that operates a cannon will not chase you, but it still goes off if you pick it up. The pink ones, Bob-omb Buddies, are friendly: they give hints and open the cannons.

from.quote: These Bob-ombs do not chase the player, but they still explode if picked up.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: A pink variant of Bob-omb called a Bob-omb Buddy is introduced in this game.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Bob-omb Buddies are friendly and give the player character helpful hints. They open cannons
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

sections.name: Chuckya (Wet-Dry World, Tall, Tall Mountain and others)

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A large purple Bob-omb variant that slides about on a metal point and charges you when you come in range; it patrols small areas in Wet-Dry World, Tall, Tall Mountain, Rainbow Ride, the huge side of Tiny-Huge Island and Bowser in the Sky.

from.quote: Chuckyas (also formatted as Chuck-Yas) are a large purple variant of Bob-omb found in Super Mario 64
from.quote_sits_at: lead (before the first heading)

from.quote: they move about by sliding across the ground on a metal point
from.quote_sits_at: lead (before the first heading)

from.quote: Chuckyas are encountered in Wet-Dry World; on Tall, Tall Mountain; in Rainbow Ride; on Tiny-Huge Island's "huge" portion; and in Bowser in the Sky
from.quote_sits_at: lead (before the first heading)

from.quote: When Mario is in range of a Chuckya, it charges towards him
from.quote_sits_at: lead (before the first heading)

from.quote: Chuckyas patrol small areas.
from.quote_sits_at: lead (before the first heading)

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: Lift it from the back and throw it; it explodes and gives up five coins.

from.quote: To defeat a Chuckya, Mario must pick it up from behind and throw it, causing it to explode and release five coins.
from.quote_sits_at: lead (before the first heading)

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: If a Chuckya grabs you it hurls you in a random direction, which can mean a long throw or a pit. Getting free takes 11 pushes of the Control Stick, each from inside to outside, before the throw.

from.quote: if a Chuckya catches him, it picks him up and throws him in a random direction
from.quote_sits_at: lead (before the first heading)

from.quote: Usually, Mario can be thrown down a far distance or even into a pit.
from.quote_sits_at: lead (before the first heading)

from.quote: It is possible to escape from a Chuckya's grasp by pressing and/or pushing the Control Stick from the inside to the outside 11 times before the Chuckya throws Mario.
from.quote_sits_at: lead (before the first heading)

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A stone slab with an angry face that patrols a small area in Whomp's Fortress and falls on you when you get near; one more waits in Bowser in the Sky.

from.quote: appear in Super Mario 64 as enemies in Whomp's Fortress
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: with a singular Whomp appearing in Bowser in the Sky
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: They are large enemies that resemble rectangular stone slabs with snaggletoothed faces
from.quote_sits_at: lead (before the first heading)

from.quote: Their faces feature permanently angry expression
from.quote_sits_at: General information > Physical description

from.quote: Whomps will patrol back and forth in a small area, attempting to slam Mario into the ground for three damage when he gets near.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: Its only weak spot is its back: let it fall flat, then ground-pound it while it lies there, and it is defeated and releases five coins.

from.quote: They can be defeated by Mario causing them to fall over and subsequently ground-pounding on their sole weak spot, their back
from.quote_sits_at: lead (before the first heading)

from.quote: Pounding the Ground on a Whomp while it lies flat will defeat it, which releases five coins.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: Stand on a Whomp's back and it gives up a coin each time you land, five at most. In the original game you can jump while it is falling, slip through it and end up on its back.

from.quote: Landing on the back of a Whomp will release a coin up to five times
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: A trick in the original version only allows Mario to pass through one and get on its back if he jumps while it falls.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

sections.name: Mr. I (Big Boo's Haunt, Lethal Lava Land, Hazy Maze Cave)

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A huge eyeball that swings round to face you and, if you leave it alone, fires little coloured bubbles your way. You find it in Big Boo's Haunt, Lethal Lava Land and Hazy Maze Cave.

from.quote: It is a giant, usually motionless eyeball that tracks the player character by rotating.
from.quote_sits_at: lead (before the first heading)

from.quote: They are found in Big Boo's Haunt, Lethal Lava Land, and the Hazy Maze Cave. They turn to face Mario, shooting small multicolored bubble projectiles at him if undisturbed.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: Circle around it: it tries to keep watching you, shrinks a little, and is beaten, leaving a blue coin.

from.quote: A Mr. I is defeated if Mario runs around it, causing the Mr. I to shrink slightly from trying to keep track and drop a Blue Coin.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: A larger Big Mr. I waits in the attic of Big Boo's Haunt.

from.quote: The larger Big Mr. I. can be found in the attic of Big Boo's Haunt.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A red metal box that rolls along set paths over a small tile maze in Shifting Sand Land, trying to flatten you.

from.quote: Tox Boxes are hollow metal boxes that roll along set paths.
from.quote_sits_at: lead (before the first heading)

from.quote: Tox Boxes are red, industrial, and metallic boxes with spray-painted faces in Super Mario 64
from.quote_sits_at: lead (before the first heading)

from.quote: they are enemies exclusive to Shifting Sand Land
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Tox Boxes attempt to flatten Mario by rolling over him. The path is a small maze of tiles surrounded by darker, faster-moving quicksand that sucks Mario in instantly.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: In the original game you cannot beat one. One face of each box is an open square: stand on a tile as the box rolls onto it and the opening spares you, but the rim around the opening still crushes anything beneath it.

from.quote: While Tox Boxes cannot be defeated in the original Super Mario 64
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: the last side is a square hole, which is for Mario to stand in as a Tox Box passes over the tile he is standing on, thus letting him survive without being crushed. However, the edges of the holed side still crush Mario if he stands under them.
from.quote_sits_at: lead (before the first heading)

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: Being squashed by a side costs three wedges of health. Long-jumping into a Tox Box's face over the quicksand loses a life at once, as if you had fallen into the quicksand. The maze has a few Red Coins and the course's only cannon.

from.quote: If Mario gets squished by a Tox Box's side, he loses three wedges of health.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Long-jumping into the side of a Tox Box's face that is above quicksand, off the side of the track, makes Mario lose a life instantly, playing the animation as if he has just fallen into the quicksand.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: The tiled maze that the Tox Boxes travel on has a few Red Coins on it, as well as the course's only cannon.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: The collectible star that clears a mission and opens more of the castle; there are 120 in the game.

from.quote: can grant Mario access to more levels in-game
from.quote_sits_at: lead (before the first heading)

from.quote: By obtaining a Power Star, the corresponding mission is cleared.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: There is a total of 120 Power Stars.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Uses
lines.text: The star doors and Big Star Doors in the castle need at least the number of Power Stars shown on them, and 70 are needed to enter Bowser in the Sky. Once you hold all 120, the cannon outside the castle opens and takes you onto its roof.

from.quote: The various ★ doors and Big Star Doors of the Mushroom Castle require Mario to have at least a certain number of Power Stars (which is displayed on normal doors).
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: A minimum of 70 Power Stars is required to access Bowser in the Sky.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Once Mario collects every Power Star, the cannon outside the Mushroom Castle becomes available for use, giving access to the castle's roof.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: Every course has seven stars, one of them earned by collecting 100 coins, and fifteen stars in the whole game are Secret Stars, kept in hidden areas or given by Toads. Collecting a course's eight red coins makes a star appear above a Star Marker.

from.quote: There are seven Power Stars in each course; one is a secret Power Star that Mario can obtain from collecting 100 coins
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Fifteen of them are Secret Stars, either found in secret areas or held by Toads.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: There are eight Red Coins in each course, and collecting all of them causes a Power Star to appear over a Star Marker.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: A star you already have shows as a translucent copy of itself, and collecting it adds nothing to your total.

from.quote: playing the level again turns the Star into a translucent version of itself
from.quote_sits_at: lead (before the first heading)

from.quote: This Star can be collected, but it does not add to the player's total Star count.
from.quote_sits_at: lead (before the first heading)

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A red coin in Super Mario 64 is worth two yellow coins, and eight of them in one area make a Power Star appear over the nearby Star Marker.

from.quote: Each of them are worth two Yellow Coins. When eight Red Coins are collected in an area, a Power Star spawns above the nearby Star Marker.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Uses
lines.text: The three cap-switch courses and the three Bowser courses each hold eight, and the two secret courses The Secret Aquarium and Wing Mario Over the Rainbow have one star each from their red coins. The Princess's Secret Slide is the only course with none.

from.quote: all three Cap Switch courses have eight Red Coins to obtain: Tower of the Wing Cap, Cavern of the Metal Cap, and Vanish Cap Under the Moat.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: This also goes for the Bowser courses: Bowser in the Dark World, Bowser in the Fire Sea, and Bowser in the Sky.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: two secret courses that each have only one Power Star from obtaining Red Coins: The Secret Aquarium and Wing Mario Over the Rainbow.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: The Princess's Secret Slide is the only course (secret or otherwise) to lack Red Coins and thus a corresponding Power Star.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Bob-omb Battlefield - Find the 8 Red Coins
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Big Boo's Haunt - Seek the 8 Red Coins
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: The rest: Dire, Dire Docks, Pole-Jumping for Red Coins; Snowman's Land, Shell Shreddin' for Red Coins; Wet-Dry World, Go to Town for Red Coins; Tall, Tall Mountain, Scary 'Shrooms, Red Coins; Tiny-Huge Island, Wiggler's Red Coins; Tick Tock Clock, Stop Time for Red Coins; Rainbow Ride, Coins Amassed in a Maze.

from.quote: Dire, Dire Docks - Pole-Jumping for Red Coins
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Snowman's Land - Shell Shreddin' for Red Coins
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Wet-Dry World - Go to Town for Red Coins
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Tall, Tall Mountain - Scary 'Shrooms, Red Coins
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Tiny-Huge Island - Wiggler's Red Coins
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Tick Tock Clock - Stop Time for Red Coins
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Rainbow Ride - Coins Amassed in a Maze
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A darker blue coin worth five yellow coins.

from.quote: Blue Coins appear in Super Mario 64 and Super Mario 64 DS, where they are depicted with a darker blue color. Blue Coins are worth five Yellow Coins when collected
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Uses
lines.text: Most come from ground-pounding a Blue Coin Block, and they last only a limited time: once the timer runs out they cannot be collected. Some defeated enemies drop one: Koopa Troopas, Piranha Plants, Boos, Mr. Is, Bookends, Pokeys and the Small Koopa Troopa, and a Grand Goomba gives one only if you kill it with a ground pound.

from.quote: they typically appear from ground-pounding a Blue Coin Block. These Blue Coins appear for a limited time and are unobtainable once the timer expires.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Defeating certain enemies causes a Blue Coin to appear, including Koopa Troopas, Piranha Plants, Boos, Mr. Is, Bookends, Pokeys, and the Small Koopa Troopa. Grand Goombas also give out a Blue Coin if killed using a Ground Pound.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: The blue coins on the slides in Cool, Cool Mountain (one) and Tall, Tall Mountain (three) start to move away from you as you get close, unlike still yellow coins.

from.quote: Blue Coins are also found in the slides on Cool, Cool Mountain (one is present) and Tall, Tall Mountain (three are present), where they start to move away from Mario once he gets close to them, in contrast to the stationary Yellow Coins.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A mushroom with a green cap and yellow spots that gives an extra life.

from.quote: 1UP Mushrooms are rendered as 2D assets depicted with green caps and yellow spots in Super Mario 64.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Grants an extra life (most appearances)
from.quote_sits_at: lead (before the first heading)

lines.label: Uses
lines.text: Reach the top of a pole, open some yellow blocks, touch a butterfly that is not an exploding one, walk into a small patch of flowers, or soar through a ring of coins.

from.quote: They are acquired through a variety of methods, such as on top of poles, in some yellow blocks, from touching butterflies that are not explosive, from a small field of flowers, or from flying through a ring of coins.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: Some stand still, some move away from you and some move at you. Three sit on the roof of the castle.

from.quote: Depending on the 1UP Mushroom, it can be either motionless, move away from Mario, or move at him. There are also three 1UP Mushrooms on the roof of the Mushroom Castle.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A rare green shell in Super Mario 64 that you can ride for fast travel.

from.quote: Koopa Shells, also referred to as shiny shells (or Shiny Shells), are rare objects in Super Mario 64. They only appear in green
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Uses
lines.text: Hop on and it carries you quickly, and enemies you ram are defeated outright. While you ride it, water, lava, quicksand and deadly quicksand cannot sink or hurt you. If you grab one underwater you can hold it out in front and swim faster for a short while.

from.quote: When Mario jumps on a Koopa Shell, he can travel at fast speed and ram into enemies to defeat them instantly. Riding a shell also allows Mario to navigate over water, lava, quicksand, and deadly quicksand without sinking or being hurt.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: if Mario grabs a Koopa Shell while underwater, he can hold the shell in front of him and use it to swim faster in water for a short period of time.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: You get one by hitting certain yellow blocks, or by attacking a Koopa Troopa until it leaves its shell. In the original game the blocks do not refill, but a shell stays until you ride it.

from.quote: can be obtained by hitting some yellow blocks or attacking a Koopa Troopa to get it out of its shell
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: In the original version, when the player hits the yellow blocks for Koopa Shells, the boxes do not respawn, but shells do not disappear until Mario hitches a ride on one.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: In the Nintendo 64 version of Tiny-Huge Island you can ride the shell on the wind over the Windswept Valley.

from.quote: in Tiny-Huge Island, Mario can use the shell to ride the wind over the Windswept Valley in the Nintendo 64 version
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: Blue cannons in ten courses and one secret stage fire you to places you cannot normally reach, but each stays covered until you find and talk to that course's Bob-omb Buddy.

from.quote: Cannons, this time colored blue, are a vital gameplay element in Super Mario 64 and Super Mario 64 DS.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: the player can use it to fire Mario to previously unreachable areas
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: There is at least one cannon found in ten levels in these games, as well as one secret stage.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: The player must successfully locate and talk to the Bob-omb Buddies in each level in order to access the cannon
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Until they do, the cannons remain covered by a metal hatch with a picture of a Bob-omb Buddy on it, and are inaccessible.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Uses
lines.text: Drop into the hole to climb in, aim with the targeting reticle and press the button to fire. Aim slightly higher than your target, and you take no falling damage from the shot. With a Wing Cap on, you can fly at once after the shot without a triple jump.

from.quote: In order to use the cannon, Mario needs to only drop down into this hole.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: a targeting reticle appears on the screen, allowing the player to aim the cannon where they want Mario to go
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: The player should aim slightly higher than the area they wish to shoot Mario to
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: Mario will not take falling damage if he is fired from a cannon.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: If the player collects a Wing Cap before entering a cannon, the player can fly around as Wing Mario immediately after being fired from the cannon, without needing to perform a Triple Jump to take off first.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: A cannon stays locked until the first mission has been completed. In Bob-omb Battlefield one cannon can never be used because it shoots water bombs.

from.quote: Cannons cannot be unlocked until after the first mission is completed.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

from.quote: In Bob-omb Battlefield, there is a cannon controlled by a Bob-omb that Mario can never access due to the cannon shooting water bombs.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: In the Whomp's Fortress mission "Blast Away the Wall" you shoot yourself out of a cannon to smash the top of a nearby wall and free the star.

from.quote: Mario must shoot himself out of a cannon in order to obliterate the topmost section of a nearby wall, which releases the hidden Power Star.
from.quote_sits_at: History > Super Mario series > Super Mario 64 / Super Mario 64 DS
